evals.name: aspire-apphost-for-two-services
evals.prompt: Write the AppHost Program.cs for two Arc services, Ordering and Billing, each with its own Chronicle event store, using Cratis.Chronicle.Aspire. Explain any setting the services need. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: One AddCratisChronicle resource with a replica-set MongoDB from AddCratisChronicleMongoDB, and per service explicit Cratis__Chronicle__ConnectionString built from the grpc endpoint, Cratis__Chronicle__EventStore, Arc MongoDB settings and WaitFor(chronicle).
assertions: Uses a single Chronicle resource for both services rather than one kernel per service.
Sets Cratis__Chronicle__ConnectionString explicitly and explains that WithReference alone supplies ConnectionStrings__chronicle, which the client does not read.
Sets a distinct Cratis__Chronicle__EventStore per service.
Uses a MongoDB replica set (AddCratisChronicleMongoDB) rather than Aspire's standalone AddMongoDB for Chronicle storage.

evals.name: compose-startup-order
evals.prompt: Give us a docker-compose layout for MongoDB, Chronicle and two Cratis services that starts in a reliable order for local development. Explain the ports. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: MongoDB as a replica set with an init job, Chronicle gated on the init job and health-checked on a dedicated health port, services gated on Chronicle health with per-service connection and store settings; publish only 35000 on 127.0.0.1 and leave 11111/30000 unpublished.
assertions: Starts MongoDB with --replSet and initiates the replica set before Chronicle starts.
Gates the services on Chronicle health using the health endpoint rather than container start alone.
Gives each service its own Cratis__Chronicle__EventStore and a connection string to the chronicle service.
Explains port 35000 versus the Orleans ports 11111 and 30000 and keeps development ports on 127.0.0.1.

evals.name: repository-layout-and-models
evals.prompt: We have Ordering, Billing and Shipping in one repository, each modeled in Screenplay. Propose the folder layout, where contracts live and where the .play files go. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: One folder per service with its own project, appsettings naming its store and frontend; a Contracts project per producer referenced by consumers; one Screenplay model folder per service, never one folder above all services because a folder is one application.
assertions: Gives each service its own folder, project, event-store setting and frontend.
Places public events in a contracts project per producer that consumers reference instead of the producer's service project.
Keeps one Screenplay model folder per service and warns that a single folder over all services merges them into one application.
